steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Advertising: paid communication through media channels (TV, radio, print, online, social media, billboards). It builds awareness and brand image but is expensive and difficult to measure ROI directly. | Key Fact: Sales promotion: short-term incentives to encourage purchase (BOGOF, discounts, coupons, free gifts, competitions). Boosts immediate sales but can damage brand image if overused. | Key Fact: Public relations (PR): managing the business's image through media coverage, press releases, events, and community involvement. It's credible (not paid for) but the business can't control the message. | Key Fact: Personal selling: one-to-one communication (sales reps, demonstrations). Effective for high-value, complex products but expensive per customer and limited reach.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain the difference between advertising and sales promotion, giving one advantage and one disadvantage of each. | Analyse why a business might choose social media marketing over traditional TV advertising. | Evaluate which promotional method would be most effective for a new luxury skincare brand targeting 25-35 year-old women.
